question.title: Will the WHO declare an H5 virus a Public Health Emergency of International Concern before 2028?
question.description:
Influenza (the flu), a viral disease with a strongly seasonal impact, comes in a number of different types. [Influenza A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Influenza_A_virus), which affects birds and certain mammals (including humans), has caused numerous pandemics throughout human history. Strains of [avian influenza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avian_influenza) (bird flu), which is caused by influenza A and primarily affects birds, are classified as either highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) or low pathogenic (LPAI), based on the severity of the virus to chickens in particular.

HPAI of the [H5N1 subtype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Influenza_A_virus_subtype_H5N1) is widespread among birds worldwide and is regarded as a serious pandemic threat. "Sporadic" human infections [have been reported](https://www.cdc.gov/bird-flu/prevention/hpai-interim-recommendations.html) in several different countries over the past few decades, in many cases in connection with exposure to diseased poultry or other farm animals, but there has never been evidence of sustained human-to-human transmission, which would be necessary for a pandemic.
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as **Yes** if before January 1, 2028, the World Health Organization declares any event caused by an H5 virus to be a Public Health Emergency of International Concern.
question.fine_print:
Per the WHO's [Q\&A documentation](https://www.who.int/news-room/questions-and-answers/item/emergencies-international-health-regulations-and-emergency-committees):

> A PHEIC is defined in the IHR (2005) as, “an extraordinary event which is determined to constitute a public health risk to other States through the international spread of disease and to potentially require a coordinated international response”. This definition implies a situation that is:

> * serious, sudden, unusual or unexpected;
> * carries implications for public health beyond the affected State’s national border; and
> * may require immediate international action.

If WHO changes this definition in a substantial manner, this question may be edited or annulled.

For purposes of this question, any subtype of H5 (e.g., H5N1, H5Nx) is acceptable if encompassed by the PHEIC.
